canonicalPackage.portableManifestNote: Agent Plugins 1.0.0 floor: root plugin.json is the portable package identity and the single version authority. Host projections (.claude-plugin, .codex-plugin, .cursor-plugin, .qoder-plugin) may add host-native fields but must not diverge on name/version. Use scripts/Bump-PackageVersion.ps1 to bump.
canonicalPackage.manifestNote: Claude-shaped host projection retained for hosts that still consume the Claude plugin layout. Version must match root plugin.json.

hosts.correctionNote: globalSkillsDir was recorded as ~/.codex/skills from the plugins page, which does not cover skill discovery. Codex's skills documentation lists REPO ($CWD/.agents/skills, $CWD/../.agents/skills, $REPO_ROOT/.agents/skills), USER ($HOME/.agents/skills), ADMIN (/etc/codex/skills) and bundled SYSTEM skills, and names no ~/.codex/skills tier. ~/.codex/config.toml remains correct for MCP and for [[skills.config]] entries.

hosts.skillsNote: Re-verified 2026-08-04 against the skills page rather than the plugins page it was originally recorded from, because that substitution is what produced three wrong globalSkillsDir values elsewhere in this registry. It holds here: ~/.factory/skills is the documented 'Personal' scope for workflows available across projects. Factory additionally reads ~/.agents/skills and ~/.agent/skills as compatibility scopes. Collapsed onto sharedSkillsDir 2026-09-02: AgentHub deploys once to ~/.agents/skills.

hosts.correctionNote: globalSkillsDir was null, verified against the agent-PLUGINS page, which does not cover skill discovery. This is the third occurrence of that exact mistake in this registry -- windsurf (verified against its MCP page) and codex (verified against its plugins page) were the first two -- so the pattern is the finding: recording a null from a page that was never about skills turns absence of evidence into evidence of absence. code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/agent-skills documents workspace .github/skills and .claude/skills plus user-home ~/.copilot/skills and ~/.claude/skills, with chat.agentSkillsLocations for custom paths. CONSEQUENCE, deliberately not acted on: both documented user-scope directories are already populated by the copilot and claude hosts, so VS Code can already see those skills; nativePaths.skillsDir for vscode-insiders is intentionally left unset, because setting it would collapse onto ~/.copilot/skills and push this host's capability set into copilot's directory. That is a deployment decision, not a documentation fix.
hosts.mcpNote: Re-verified 2026-08-04: VS Code's top-level MCP key is "servers", NOT "mcpServers" as every other JSON-file host in this fleet uses. Sync-AgentHub.ps1 already passes -JsonProperty 'servers' for this host.

hosts.note: A native .devin-plugin manifest is optional because Devin documents Claude-package fallback.
OpenCode plugins are executable JavaScript or TypeScript hooks, not capability bundle manifests.

hosts.correctionNote: globalSkillsDir was ~/.warp/skills. That path is real and still documented, but recording it alone understated what the same page says: Warp mirrors its multi-tool project search at root scope and names ~/.agents/skills first as recommended. Warp is the only host in this fleet that reads other hosts' skill directories, so a private ~/.warp/skills copy duplicated skills Warp could already see via ~/.claude/skills and the rest. alsoScannedSkillsDirs records the full documented set so a future reader does not have to re-derive it.

globalSkillsDir was recorded as null because the earlier research verified windsurf against its MCP page, which says nothing about skills; absence of evidence on an unrelated page became evidence of absence. Windsurf's own skills page documents three scopes -- Workspace .windsurf/skills/, Global ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/, and System (Enterprise) -- so the ~31 skills deployed at that path are reachable, not inert. This reversed a planned prune of them.

fieldNotes.globalSkillsDir: Home-scope skills directory the host actually reads. null means the host documents project-scope skills only, so a home-directory deployment is inert.
fieldNotes.subagents: How the host consumes subagent role files. 'unverified' means the host's documentation was not confirmed; do not assume the AgentHub agents/ tree loads there.
fieldNotes.mcpKey: Property (JSON) or section shape (TOML/YAML) that holds MCP server entries.
fieldNotes.multiDirectoryReaders: Warp and Amp both scan several home skill directories, so per-host skill copies are enumerated repeatedly by those two hosts. See fleetNotes.

fleetNotes: Warp reads ~/.agents/skills, ~/.warp/skills, ~/.claude/skills, ~/.codex/skills, ~/.cursor/skills, ~/.gemini/skills, ~/.copilot/skills, ~/.factory/skills, ~/.github/skills, and ~/.opencode/skills. With one copy deployed per host, Warp enumerated 185 entries for 53 distinct skills on 2026-08-03. Collapsed 2026-09-02 onto ~/.agents/skills as the master library; hosts that cannot read that path use a junction from their documented skillsDir.

Amp skill precedence is ~/.config/agents/skills, then ~/.agents/skills, then ~/.config/amp/skills. Collapsed 2026-09-02 onto ~/.agents/skills (sharedSkillsDir) so Amp, Warp, Cline, Gemini, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, Factory, and Windsurf share one deploy.

CORRECTED 2026-08-20. This note previously read 'windsurf has no documented global skills directory; the managed deployment under ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills is inert.' That was false. Windsurf documents three skill scopes -- workspace .windsurf/skills/, global ~/.codeium/windsurf/skills/, and system/enterprise -- so the 33 skills deployed at that path are reachable. The original claim came from verifying windsurf against its MCP docs page, which says nothing about skills; absence of evidence on an unrelated page became evidence of absence. Commit 2138f305 (2026-08-04) fixed hosts[].windsurf.globalSkillsDir and added its correctionNote, but left this line untouched, so the file asserted both halves at once for sixteen days. Nothing in the repo reads fleetNotes -- Sync-Capabilities.ps1 prunes from agents.json, not this file -- so no code would have acted on the stale half; the exposure was a human or agent trusting this prose and pruning 33 live skill directories by hand.
Neither Sync-AgentHub.ps1 nor Sync-Capabilities.ps1 deploys subagents. agentsDir is never a deployment target, so loose-skill hosts receive skills but no agents/ roles.
